The translation vector is the image minus the object.

\(x: -8 - (-3) = -5\)

\(y: 15 - (8) = 7\)

So the vector is \(\begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ 7 \end{pmatrix}\).

text: Find the image of the point \((2, -6)\) under an enlargement with centre the origin and scale factor 3.
explanation:
Multiply both coordinates by the scale factor 3.

\(3 \times 2 = 6\)

\(3 \times -6 = -18\)

So the image is \((6, -18)\).

text: Find the image of the point \((-4, 0)\) under the translation \(\begin{pmatrix} -3 \\ -8 \end{pmatrix}\).
explanation:
Add the translation vector to the position vector of the point.

\(x: -4 + (-3) = -7\)

\(y: 0 + (-8) = -8\)

So the image is \((-7, -8)\).

text: Find the image of the point \((9, -4)\) under the translation \(\begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix}\).
explanation:
Add the translation vector to the position vector of the point.

\(x: 9 + (5) = 14\)

\(y: -4 + (-4) = -8\)

So the image is \((14, -8)\).

text: A translation maps the point \((-4, -4)\) onto \((-2, 3)\). Find the translation vector.
explanation:
The translation vector is the image minus the object.

\(x: -2 - (-4) = 2\)

\(y: 3 - (-4) = 7\)

So the vector is \(\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 7 \end{pmatrix}\).

text: Find the image of the point \((7, 5)\) under a rotation of 90° anticlockwise about the origin.
explanation:
Under a rotation of 90° anticlockwise about the origin, \((x, y) \rightarrow (-y, x)\).

So \((7, 5) \rightarrow (-5, 7)\).

text: Find the image of the point \((8, 2)\) under an enlargement with centre the origin and scale factor -3.
explanation:
Multiply both coordinates by the scale factor -3.

\(-3 \times 8 = -24\)

\(-3 \times 2 = -6\)

So the image is \((-24, -6)\).

text: Find the image of the point \((-5, -7)\) under a rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin.
explanation:
Under a rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin, \((x, y) \rightarrow (y, -x)\).

So \((-5, -7) \rightarrow (-7, 5)\).

text: Find the image of the point \((5, -5)\) under an enlargement with centre the origin and scale factor -3.
explanation:
Multiply both coordinates by the scale factor -3.

\(-3 \times 5 = -15\)

\(-3 \times -5 = 15\)

So the image is \((-15, 15)\).

text: Find the image of the point \((-7, 5)\) under a rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin.
explanation:
Under a rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin, \((x, y) \rightarrow (y, -x)\).

So \((-7, 5) \rightarrow (5, 7)\).

text: Find the image of the point \((-7, -2)\) under the translation \(\begin{pmatrix} -4 \\ -7 \end{pmatrix}\).
explanation:

\(x: -7 + (-4) = -11\)

\(y: -2 + (-7) = -9\)

So the image is \((-11, -9)\).

text: Find the image of the point \((3, -8)\) under the translation \(\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}\).
explanation:

\(x: 3 + (4) = 7\)

\(y: -8 + (-2) = -10\)

text: A translation maps the point \((-2, -6)\) onto \((-3, -4)\). Find the translation vector.
explanation:
The translation vector is the image minus the object.

\(x: -3 - (-2) = -1\)

\(y: -4 - (-6) = 2\)

So the vector is \(\begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}\).

text: Find the image of the point \((3, -9)\) under a rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin.
explanation:
Under a rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin, \((x, y) \rightarrow (y, -x)\).

So \((3, -9) \rightarrow (-9, -3)\).

text: Find the image of the point \((-4, 6)\) under a reflection in the origin.
explanation:
Reflection in the origin changes the sign of both coordinates.

So \((-4, 6) \rightarrow (4, -6)\).

text: Find the image of the point \((-4, 6)\) under a reflection in the x-axis.
explanation:
Reflection in the x-axis keeps \(x\) and changes the sign of \(y\).

So \((-4, 6) \rightarrow (-4, -6)\).
